report:
**Conclusion: Yes, regular intake of cranberry products can help prevent recurrent cystitis (UTIs) in women, though the benefit is moderate rather than dramatic.**

**Evidence Summary:**

The strongest evidence comes from the **2023 Cochrane review** (50 RCTs, 8,857 participants), which found that cranberry products significantly reduced the risk of symptomatic, culture-verified UTIs. For women with recurrent UTIs specifically, the risk reduction was approximately **26%** (RR ~0.70 overall, ~0.53 in recurrent-UTI women in some analyses). This was confirmed by a **2024 AFP evidence summary** concluding that cranberry products—whether juice, tablets, or capsules—“likely decrease the risk of UTI in women with recurrent UTI.”

A **2024 network meta-analysis** (20 trials, 3,000+ participants) further found cranberry juice reduced UTI rates and antibiotic use by ~49% compared to placebo.

**Mechanism:** Cranberries contain **proanthocyanidins (PACs)** that prevent *E. coli* from adhering to the bladder wall. A dose of **36 mg PACs** is cited as the specific effective dose.

**Important caveats:**
- Evidence has historically been mixed, with some older individual trials showing no effect, leading to earlier uncertainty.
- Cranberry products are for **prevention**, not treatment of active infections.
- Benefit appears limited to susceptible populations (women with recurrent UTIs, children, post-medical-intervention patients); no clear benefit was seen in pregnant women or elderly care-home residents.
- Efficacy depends on PAC content and product formulation.

**Sources:**

- https://www.aafp.org/afp/2024/0700/mbtn-cranberry-products-urinary-tract-infections.pdf
- https://posts.terabox.com/hub/2023-and-2024-cochrane-review-findings-on-cranberry-products-for-preventing-urinary-tract-infections
- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2405456924001226
